title: Higher direct images as sheafified cohomology presheaves
statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For an object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ write $H^q(U,F)$ for the $q$-th right derived functor, evaluated at $F$, of the left exact functor $\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab$, $G\mapsto G(U)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive] (computed from an injective resolution of $F$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]). For an etale $V\to S$ the base change $X\times_SV\to X$ is etale, hence an object of $X_{\Et}$, and a morphism $g:V'\to V$ of $S_{\Et}$ gives the morphism $\mathrm{id}_X\times g:X\times_SV'\to X\times_SV$ of $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; the restriction map $H^q(X\times_SV,F)\to H^q(X\times_SV',F)$ is the map induced on $H^q$ by the restriction maps $I^\bullet(X\times_SV)\to I^\bullet(X\times_SV')$ of an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. Then for every $q\geq0$ the higher direct image $R^qp_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is canonically isomorphic to the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf on $S_{\Et}$

$$
 V\longmapsto H^q(X\times_SV,F).
$$

No hypothesis (quasi-compactness, separatedness) is put on $p$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), applied to the morphism of sites $X_{\Et}\to S_{\Et}$ given by the continuous functor $u(V)=X\times_SV$ with $\mathcal O=\underline{\mathbf Z}$ (so that modules are abelian sheaves); the passage from the K-injective definition of $Rp_*$ to an injective resolution is lem-sp-kinjective-computes (2)

proof.text: Choose the Mathlib injective resolution R of F. Abelian sheaves on the small etale site form a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], hence have enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Put f=p_*, K=f(R.cocomplex) and L=iota(K), where iota is inclusion into presheaves. InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj computes the classical derived functor using R [def-sp-injective-resolutions; def-sp-left-exact-additive; lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso identifies the total bounded-below derived value on F[0] with the classical right-derived value [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus no separate choice or comparison of arbitrary K-injective resolutions is needed.

proof.text: For V in S_et, evaluation of L at V is definitionally evaluation of R.cocomplex at the base-change object X times_S V, since p_* is precomposition by the base-change functor [def-weil-pbc-direct-image; lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The same definitional identification holds for differentials and restriction maps.

proof.text: Construct an isomorphism eP from the specified presheaf P_q to the presheaf homology H^q(L). Its component at V is R.isoRightDerivedObj for evaluation at X times_S V followed by ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso for evaluation at V. Evaluation preserves limits and colimits pointwise in a functor category, hence preserves homology [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. For a restriction g, rewrite its derived map by InjectiveResolution.rightDerived_app_eq [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], cancel the resolution comparison isomorphism, and apply ShortComplex.homologyMap_mapNatTrans to the evaluation natural transformation. This proves naturality of eP, including the specified derived restriction maps.

proof.text: Sheafification a is exact [def-weil-pbc-sheafification; lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. The inverse of sheafificationNatIso gives a termwise natural isomorphism a(iota(K)) to K; lift it to complexes with Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso and Functor.mapHomologicalComplexIdIso, obtaining eK. ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso for a identifies a(H^q(L)) with H^q(a(L)) [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Mapping eK under homology then identifies this with H^q(K).

proof.text: Compose a.mapIso eP, the inverse homology comparison for a, homology applied to eK, the inverse of R.isoRightDerivedObj f q, and the inverse of f.homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso F q. This is the required isomorphism from the sheafification of P_q to H^q(Rp_*(F[0])). All components are the canonical resolution or homology comparisons; the restriction naturality was verified in step 3.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks sites-cohomology Lemma 072W and its proof (read in literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex:747-782), into five steps: (1) an injective resolution exists (Ab(X_et) Grothendieck abelian, enough injectives) and is K-injective, so R^qp_*F = H^q(p_*I) by def-weil-pbc-direct-image, independent of the resolution; (2) (p_*I)(V) = I(X x_S V) by definition, with restriction maps; (3) H^q(I(X x_S V)) = H^q(X x_S V, F) by the definition of H^q(U,-) as derived functors of G -> G(U) on Ab(X_et) (Stacks 21.2), with the restriction maps of Stacks 21.7 (equation-restriction-mapping) -- no restriction-of-injectives argument (03F3) is needed since H^q(U,F) is defined on Ab(X_et); (4) the cohomology sheaf of a complex of abelian sheaves is the sheafification of the presheaf cohomology, from lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact (Mathlib leaf) and lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology (Mathlib leaf) and the counit iso; (5) conclusion. Statement: 'morphism of schemes' repointed from def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions to def-pc-scheme; the restriction maps of the presheaf V -> H^q(X x_S V, F) and the functor V -> X x_S V (lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits) are now stated explicitly. No new nodes; Mathlib searched three ways again: no higher direct images on sites.
